metadata.title: Guidance ('Guidelines') for Evaluation of Hysteroscopic Sterilization Devices
metadata.topic: Guidance · FDA devices, foods, veterinary and tobacco
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: A. Description of Device and Technique The applicant should provide detailed diagrams and descriptions of the device and its applicator. Where appropriate, samples of the devices should be available for examination. The physical characteristics of the device should be indicated and the rationale for the design should be stated in light of the relevant literature.

B. Physical Properties (material, where appropriate, to be tested before and after sterilization process) As appropriate, engineering tests should be performed and the results considered relative to physical properties as well as design and rationale.

candidates.statement: II. Clinical Guidelines Prior to clinical testing, it must be documented that appropriate toxicology and animal studies for the proposed clinical trial have been done. Animal findings relevant to the safety of hysteroscopic sterilization devices will be completed prior to initiation of phase II clinical studies.
candidates.context: Investigations of this nature are to be conducted in such a way that the participating subjects or patients are exposed to the least possible risk consistent with the anticipated benefit.
